## Ledger Conventions

D425 check selection in AGENTS.md applies to every card, including older broad test/build/system/runtime/reload packets: select only affected checks at the current stage and record deferred coverage. Historical receipts are not commands to replay; unchanged source/configuration reuses passing evidence. D423 forbids full-suite triggers on session changes and permits independent work while full acceptance is pending.

D375 applies to all existing cards, including older paragraphs requesting full frontend or broad backend checks per slice: coverage is preserved, but execution follows AGENTS.md focused/feature/app-ready timing. Record deferred required check commands/scope and trigger on the card/checkpoint; keep that acceptance unfinished. Implemented, focused-checked prerequisites can support further local coding with their verification limits recorded. Required security/source review follows focused checks, and D376 requires actual source-read evidence before claiming independent review.

- Heading format: `ID — title [status]`. Allowed states: `pending`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `done`, `deferred`. Update this field when work starts/stops; keep completion evidence in the checkpoint journal.
- **Needs** lists blocking implementation prerequisites. A comma means all listed dependencies; `or` means an explicit alternative. “As available” is an incremental attachment, not permission to mark absent required functionality done.
- Phase source references use sections of [PROJECT_PLAN.md](PROJECT_PLAN.md), accepted D-numbers from [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md), and the same phase in TODO. SEO/SaaS markers require the corresponding rules and reference maps routed in the guide.
- Proposed code locations are responsibilities, not pre-existing filenames. Use `backend/`, `frontend/`, `deploy/` and CI directories once created; record actual files and commands in the checkpoint. Create models only with their working feature.
- **Build** describes the implementation slice; **Check** is mandatory task-specific acceptance in addition to the common contract. Split oversized cards into stable suffixed IDs rather than declaring partial work complete.
- D103 separates code from provider/production release evidence. Implement complete credential-entry and selection UI, provider/billing flows, downstream SEO features and deployment artifacts against official contracts and local fixture/synthetic checks without requesting real accounts, model choices, example domains or AWS access. A mock proves code behavior, not actual provider capability; P3A-12/P3A-13/P13-05 and capability-specific live gates retain their real checks. Record unrun evidence, not a coding stop. Never activate paid/public claims or bypass tenant/security/approval boundaries.
- A card is an acceptance unit, not a session limit. After completion, follow [CONTINUE.md](../CONTINUE.md) and the guide's execution lanes to the next dependency-ready authorized card; no fixed card limit applies unless the user specifies a narrower task/batch (D068).

### P04-02 — Transaction-safe dispatch and recoverable execution [done]

- **Needs:** P04-01.
- **Build:** Dispatch after DB commit to explicit default/AI/crawl/audit queues. Define stable idempotency, bounded transient-only retries, soft/hard timeouts and redacted errors. Handle DB commit followed by broker failure with recoverable undispatched state/reconciliation; duplicate deliveries cannot duplicate side effects. Snapshot prompt/output versions and safe provider IDs when available.
- **Check:** Transaction rollback never queues work; simulated broker failure recovers the persisted job. Duplicate delivery, worker crash/restart and transient/permanent failures leave correct authoritative state. External operations require provider idempotency/reconciliation before retry, not only a local task flag.
- **Verified evidence:** D070. A project/handler/key uniqueness constraint and actor/input/config match enforce idempotency. Post-commit default-queue publish records dispatched timestamp or fixed broker-failure category; bounded DB-row-locked reconciliation handles pending/stale outcomes. The DEBUG-only diagnostic Celery task uses late ack, bounded time limits and job-row serialization; tests cover rollback, broker outage/recovery, stale/duplicate delivery, concurrent same-key requests, revocation, fixed-category failure and crash-mid-step rollback/recovery. `jobs.0002` applied only to dev; real Redis/default-worker complete/partial/duplicate delivery and owned fixture cleanup passed. Full78 PostgreSQL tests/system/current/drift and9 check-tool tests passed, then the focused crash regression passed. No external provider operation is retryable without its future provider-owned idempotency/reconciliation contract.

Validate schemes/ports/DNS/IPs at connection and redirect boundaries; block private, loopback, link-local and metadata destinations, including IPv6 and rebinding cases.
